sources.name: SPEC CPU 2017 published results
sources.licence: SPEC Fair Use Rules (https://www.spec.org/products/fairuse). Public use is allowed when the source and retrieval date are stated, the licensee of each result is identifiable, the SPEC trademarks are acknowledged, SPEC metrics are compared only with SPEC metrics of the same benchmark release, and derived values and estimates are clearly labelled and never called SPEC metrics. The site does all of these.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; SPEC publishes new results about every two weeks
sources.typical_lag: results appear weeks to months after the test date

limitations: SPEC results are submitted by hardware vendors and are dominated by servers.
Each result is one tested configuration: memory, compiler and operating system differ between results for the same processor.
Scores are SPECrate 2017 Integer base. No other suite or metric is mixed in.
Predicted scores and residuals are this site's estimates derived from SPEC results. They are not SPEC metrics and were not produced by SPEC-compliant runs.
SPEC, SPEC CPU and SPECrate are registered trademarks of the Standard Performance Evaluation Corporation. The licensee behind each result is named in its SPEC disclosure, linked from every row.
meta.target: log of SPECrate 2017 Integer base score

verdict.statement: AutoGluon: WeightedEnsemble_L2 beats the cores-times-clock baseline on the newest generation by more than the spread between folds.

finding.label: prediction
finding.reason: The published model predicts scores for the newest processor generation, which it never saw, better than the cores-times-clock baseline by more than the fold-to-fold spread.
